sources.says: On an appeal, a tie vote sustains the chair’s decision, even if the chair’s own vote created the tie, because the decision can be reversed only by a majority.
A member has no right to explain their vote during voting, since that would amount to debate at that point.

q1428.answer: Because it would be the same as debating.

sources.says: No single member can force a count. A member who thinks a count is needed should move that the vote be counted, and the motion requires a majority.

q1429.answer: Move that the vote be counted.

sources.says: Bylaws may require ballot votes, as in elections and admission to membership. Any vote on charges before or after a trial should always be by ballot.
Any vote related to charges before or after a trial should be by ballot. A ballot vote can otherwise be ordered by majority vote.
When a vote is by ballot, no action is in order that would force disclosure of a member’s vote.

q1431.answer: A vote related to charges after a member’s trial should be by ballot.

sources.says: The presiding officer may vote by ballot along with other members, but if the chair doesn’t vote before the polls close, it takes the assembly’s permission.
It’s usually best to rely on the chair to close the polls.

q1432.answer: The false statement is that the chair may vote after the polls close without permission.

sources.says: After the polls are closed, a majority vote is required to reopen them.
A representative body should set the size of the minority that can order a roll call, for example one-fifth of those present, as in Congress.
In a roll call vote, those in favor answer “aye,” “yes,” or “yea.”
In a roll call vote, those opposed answer “no” or “nay.”
Except in a ballot vote, a member may change their vote up until the result is announced. After that, it takes unanimous consent.
In a roll call vote, a record of how each member voted, along with the result, is entered in full in the minutes.

q1438.answer: How each member voted is recorded in the minutes.

sources.says: At a mass meeting, the chairman is commonly nominated by the person designated to call the meeting to order.

q1439.answer: The person who called the meeting to order.

sources.says: When the chair calls for nominations from the floor, a member rises and says “I nominate Mr. A.” No second is required.
The nominating committee should be elected by the organization when possible, or else by its executive board. In an organized society, the president shouldn’t appoint it or serve on it.

q1441.answer: The organization or its executive board.

sources.says: When the nominating committee reports is decided by the rules or established custom of the particular organization.
A motion to close nominations requires a two-thirds vote, because it takes away members’ right to nominate.
Nominations can be reopened by a majority vote.
A candidate who wins a majority for more than one office on a single ballot must, if present, choose which office to accept. If absent, the assembly decides by ballot.
The presiding officer’s station is called “the chair,” and whoever is presiding is also referred to as “the chair.”
The presiding officer’s duties include announcing business in proper sequence, enforcing the rules of debate, and deciding all questions of order, subject to appeal, unless in doubt.

q1447.answer: Letting the assembly decide all questions of order is not the chair’s duty. The chair decides them, subject to appeal.

sources.says: Bylaws that provide for a president-elect usually also provide that the president-elect precedes the first vice-president in the right to preside.

q1448.answer: A president-elect, if the bylaws provide for one.

sources.says: An elected chairman pro tem’s office ends when the president or a vice-president enters, or when the assembly adopts a motion to declare the chair vacant and elect a new chairman.
When the bylaws provide for a president-elect, a member who serves a full term as president-elect automatically becomes president.

When the president resigns, dies, or is removed, the first vice-president automatically becomes president. Likewise, when a vice-president’s place opens, the lower-ranking vice-presidents move up in order.
A historian prepares a narrative account of the society’s activities during their term, which becomes part of the official history when the assembly approves it.
A sergeant-at-arms is sometimes called a warden or warrant officer. A curator is a separate officer who looks after objects of value belonging to the society.
A doorkeeper or guard checks the credentials of those arriving at meetings limited to members and keeps out unauthorized people.
Directors should always be elected. Other officers are usually elected, but the bylaws may provide for their appointment.
An honorary office isn’t really an office but a complimentary title that may be given to members or nonmembers.

q1456.answer: All three statements are true, so none is false.

sources.says: Honorary presidents and vice-presidents should sit on the platform, but they don’t preside.
If an organization needs a parliamentarian, the president should be free to appoint one they trust. The board or society must approve any fee.

The president should confer with the parliamentarian before meetings and during recesses to anticipate problems and avoid frequent consultation during meetings. A permanent parliamentarian has no set number of extra duties.

q1459.answer: The presiding officer should confer with the parliamentarian before the meeting.

sources.says: After the parliamentarian gives an opinion, the chair makes the final ruling and may follow or disregard the advice.

q1460.answer: The chair may disregard the advice.

sources.says: The official record of a deliberative assembly’s proceedings is usually called the minutes, or sometimes, especially in legislative bodies, the journal.
The first paragraph of the minutes gives the kind of meeting, the name of the society, the date, time, and place, and whether the regular chairman and secretary were present.

q1462.answer: Whether the regular president and secretary were present.

sources.says: The first paragraph includes the society’s name, the date and time, and the place if it varies, along with a few other details. It doesn’t list how members voted.

q1463.answer: The names of members who voted to approve the previous minutes.

sources.says: Minutes should mainly record what was done at the meeting, not what was said. They must never reflect the secretary’s opinion, favorable or otherwise.

q1464.answer: The secretary’s opinions on adopted motions.

sources.says: The proceedings of a committee of the whole aren’t entered in the minutes. The fact that the assembly went into committee of the whole and the committee’s report are recorded.

q1465.answer: The proceedings of the committee of the whole.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: Proceedings under informal consideration are recorded in the assembly’s minutes as they would be under the regular rules.
Minutes record mainly what was done at the meeting, not what members said.
When the assembly orders a report “to be entered in the minutes,” the secretary copies it in full into the minutes or attaches a copy.

q1467.answer: Copy the entire report into the minutes.

sources.says: Minutes should be signed by the secretary, and the president may also sign if the assembly wishes.
The words “Respectfully submitted” are an older practice that isn’t essential when signing minutes.
Minutes are a record of what was done at the meeting.
When the chair appoints a committee, the appointment takes effect when the chair announces the names of the members to the assembly.

q1470.answer: The names of the committee members appointed by the chair, since announcing them is part of the action taken.

sources.says: In a session lasting more than a day, the previous day’s minutes are read and approved at the beginning of each day’s business after the first.

q1471.answer: At the beginning of each day’s business.

sources.says: When proceedings are published, they often include, beyond the ordinary minutes, a list of speakers on each side of every question with an abstract or the text of each speech.
A treasurer’s report at a regular meeting may be simply a statement of the cash balance on hand, or that balance less outstanding obligations. It requires no action.
A board can act only at a properly called meeting with a quorum. Approval obtained separately by phone, interviews, or in writing isn’t valid action, even from every member.
Action taken on such separately obtained approval is among the cases that can be ratified at a valid meeting.

q1474.answer: It must be ratified at the next regular board meeting.

sources.says: In small boards, the chairman, if a member, may speak in informal discussion and debate, and vote on all questions, without leaving the chair, and need not rise.

q1475.answer: The chair can speak without rising or leaving the chair.

sources.says: A committee is one or more persons, elected or appointed, to consider, investigate, or act on certain matters. Unlike a board, a committee isn’t considered a form of assembly.

q1476.answer: The false statement is that a committee is a form of assembly.

sources.says: In an ordinary society, standing committee members serve a term matching the officers’, or until successors are chosen, unless the bylaws provide otherwise.

q1477.answer: The same term as the officers.

sources.says: A special committee is also called a select or ad hoc committee. It’s appointed for a specific task and ceases to exist once it gives its final report.

q1478.answer: Standing. Special, select, and ad hoc are the same kind.

sources.says: A special committee appointed to carry out an order of the assembly should be small and include only those in favor of the action. Anyone not in sympathy should ask to be excused.

q1479.answer: Members who favor carrying out the action.

sources.says: In small committees, the chairman usually acts as secretary. In large committees, a secretary may be chosen to keep a brief memorandum, like minutes, for the committee’s use.

q1480.answer: A brief memorandum for the committee’s use.

sources.says: A committee may hold a hearing where society members present their views, but during the committee’s actual deliberations only committee members have the right to be present.
The motion to “rise” is never used in standing committees, or in special committees until they are ready to make their final report.
Standing committees serve terms matching the officers’ and are generally required to report at least once a year, usually at the annual meeting.

q1483.answer: At least once a year, at the annual meeting.

sources.says: A committee’s report is presented by a “reporting member.” For a committee, this is the chairman, unless the chairman doesn’t agree with the report or is unable to present it.
If the person presenting the report doesn’t make the motion to implement its recommendations, any member of the assembly may, but the motion must then be seconded.
For committee reports, “adopt,” “accept,” and “agree to” mean the same thing, but “adopt” is usually best because it’s least likely to be misunderstood.
A board report should be signed only by the president or chairman of the board and its secretary.

q1487.answer: The president and secretary of the board.

sources.says: A special committee report opens with forms like “The committee to which was referred… reports that…” or “The committee appointed to… reports that…” or “…submits the following report.”
Committee reports are worded in the third person, as the report of the committee.

q1488.answer: “The committee has studied… and we have decided that…” is not correct.

sources.says: A written committee report of considerable importance should be signed by all the members who concur.
If a question is referred while a motion to postpone it indefinitely is pending, that motion is ignored by the committee and by the assembly when the committee reports.

q1490.answer: The motion to Postpone Indefinitely isn’t taken up when the committee reports.

sources.says: Complex amendments are written out or submitted in a formal written report. The report can include the resolution in full, followed by the proposed amendments, and a single motion can adopt them all.

q1491.answer: The false statement is that the resolution should follow the proposed amendments. It comes first.

sources.says: A report containing only information, such as an account of work done, should be in writing. Apart from filing it, no action is needed, and usually none should be taken.

q1492.answer: It is filed, and no action should be taken.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: The assembly votes to go into committee of the whole and a chairman is appointed. The committee considers the matter, adopts a report, then rises and reports to the assembly.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: A committee of the whole is a real committee, so while the meeting is in committee of the whole it isn’t technically the assembly.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: A committee of the whole can’t adjourn or recess. It must rise so the assembly can do so.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: In committee of the whole, a point of order, an appeal, and a division of the assembly are all in order, along with motions to adopt, amend, and rise.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: The only motions in order in committee of the whole are to adopt, to amend, and to rise, plus certain incidental motions such as a point of order, an appeal, and a division.

q1495.answer: An appeal from the decision of the chair.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: A committee of the whole can’t appoint subcommittees or refer matters to another committee. Appeals must be voted on directly, it can’t discipline members, and only the chair can order a counted rising vote.

q1496.answer: The false statement is that a committee of the whole can refer a matter to another committee.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: Quasi committee of the whole is a simpler version of the committee of the whole, convenient in medium-sized assemblies. It isn’t a real committee; it’s the assembly acting as if in committee of the whole.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: The presiding officer doesn’t appoint a chairman, but stays in the chair throughout. The secretary keeps only a temporary memo of what happens, and the minutes record just the report from the quasi committee and the action taken on it.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: The motion to rise isn’t used. When no more amendments are offered, the presiding officer reports to the assembly and states the question on the amendments.

q1497.answer: The presiding officer remains in the chair throughout.

sources.says: Before a mass meeting, sponsors should agree on their choice for chairman, who will call the meeting to order, who will be nominated for secretary and by whom, what rules to propose, and who will explain the meeting’s purpose.
A mass meeting chairman should be a competent presiding officer and in sympathy with the meeting’s object. It helps if they personally know many attendees.
Admittance to a mass meeting can be limited to the invited category, and no others need be admitted if the sponsors so choose.
When only those invited are admitted, a person discovered to have entered improperly can be asked to leave.
The call of a mass meeting, stating its purpose and who is invited, has force like bylaws. It defines what motions are in order and who may participate, whatever rules the meeting adopts.
A mass meeting may adopt rules, such as ones changing the length and number of speeches.

q1501.answer: The false statement is that attendees may change the meeting’s original purpose.

sources.says: A mass meeting’s chairman and secretary are elected immediately after the meeting is called to order, conveniently by voice vote.

q1502.answer: Right after the first meeting is called to order.

sources.says: In a voice-vote election the first nominee is voted on first, so the sponsors’ choice should be nominated first for each office. Other nominations may be made from the floor.

q1503.answer: The sponsors’ choice should be nominated first for each office.

sources.says: After the elections, the chair says, “The Secretary will now read the call of this meeting.”
If resolutions weren’t prepared in advance, a committee should be appointed at the meeting to draft them.

q1505.answer: A committee should be appointed at the meeting to draft them.

sources.says: After a motion to appoint a committee to draft bylaws, the next step is a motion fixing the date, hour, and place of the next meeting, where the bylaws committee will report.

q1506.answer: Fix the date, hour, and place of the next meeting.

sources.says: Even when committee members do the drafting, a parliamentarian can often be of great help as a consultant.
The bylaws committee may consult an attorney about legal requirements, and if the society is to be incorporated, the attorney drafts the charter.
Copies of the proposed bylaws should be prepared for everyone entering the second organizational meeting.
At the second organizational meeting, the bylaws committee’s report is normally received after the minutes are approved. A proposed corporate charter, if any, is presented first.
After the recess to enroll members, the chairman pro tem calls for the reading of the roll of members. Then come the nomination and election of permanent officers.
A committee to draw up proposed bylaws is usually appointed at the first organizational meeting of a new society.
A revision replaces the whole set of bylaws. It is handled like any other bylaw amendment.
The requirements for amending the bylaws should be specified in the bylaws themselves.

q1511.answer: Three-fourths, the vote the existing bylaws require for amendment.

sources.says: Articles of bylaws are commonly numbered with Roman numerals, and sections with Arabic numerals.
The article on officers names the offices the society requires and how they are filled, not the people holding them. Typical articles also include Name, Object, and Members.

q1513.answer: “Officers’ Names.” Bylaws list offices, not the names of officeholders.

sources.says: The parliamentary authority article is one sentence saying that the rules in the current edition of a specified standard parliamentary manual govern the society where applicable and not inconsistent with its own rules.

q1514.answer: Naming a specific parliamentary manual to govern the society.

sources.says: A motion to amend the bylaws is a particular case of Amend Something Previously Adopted, so it is a main motion.
An affirmative vote on a motion to amend the bylaws can’t be reconsidered. Otherwise it follows the rules for main motions.

q1516.answer: An affirmative vote on it can’t be reconsidered.

sources.says: The final vote on a bylaw amendment should be counted and recorded in the minutes unless it is nearly unanimous.

q1517.answer: Be counted and recorded in the minutes.

sources.says: Amendments to a proposed bylaw amendment can be first or second degree and adopted by majority vote without notice, but they are limited in how much change they propose.
When notice is required, no amendment is in order that increases the change beyond what notice was given for.

q1518.answer: They can’t increase the change to the article beyond what was noticed.

sources.says: Notice of a bylaw amendment is usually given under new business, but it can be given at any time, even after a vote to adjourn if the chair hasn’t yet declared the meeting adjourned.
If a constituent unit’s president can’t attend the convention, the vice-president takes the president’s place.
Registered alternates usually get badges of a different color or shape and are seated in sections apart from delegates.

A delegate who accepts election must attend the convention and shouldn’t leave it to an alternate except for serious reason. At the convention the delegate must attend business meetings and be ready to report to the unit afterward.
“Caucus” is sometimes applied to a meeting of all known supporters of a position on an important issue, who meet to plan strategy within the assembly.

q1523.answer: A strategy meeting of avowed supporters of an issue.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: The Resolutions Committee screens and recommends action on resolutions and original main motions coming before the convention.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: The Credentials Committee’s duties include arranging for registration at the convention and handling the registration itself.

q1525.answer: Arranging for registration at the convention.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: In a convention lasting several days, registration may begin one or two days before the convention opens.

q1526.answer: One or two days before the convention begins.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: Convention standing rules often modify rules of the parliamentary authority, and their effect expires at the close of the session that adopted them.

q1527.answer: They end when the session that adopted them adjourns.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: The Program Committee plans and submits the proposed schedule of meetings, proceedings, and special events of the convention.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: Convention committee reports that are informational and need no action should, as far as possible, be taken up in succession at the same point in the order of business.

q1529.answer: In succession at the same place in the order of business.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: A time for announcements should come right before the adjournment of each convention meeting.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: Starting the second day, the minutes of the previous day’s meetings are read immediately after any opening ceremonies at the first meeting of each day.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: Authority to approve convention minutes is usually delegated to the board or a special committee, by standing rule or resolution.
When the assembly will be dissolved, as at a convention’s final meeting, unapproved minutes should be approved before adjournment or approval delegated to the board or a special committee.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: A formal installation of officers, if any, is often part of a closing banquet meeting.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: The Convention Arrangements Committee is appointed by the board to handle the convention’s physical arrangements.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: The committee may be empowered to consult experts, including professional convention managers.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: Its duties may be delegated to subcommittees or divided among separate committees.

q1534.answer: All three statements are true, so none is false.

sources.says: Penalties a society can impose generally include censure, a fine (if the bylaws allow), suspension, or expulsion, which is the most extreme.

q1535.answer: None of them. All three may be imposed.

sources.says: The chair should stay calm in dealing with disorder and should never try to drown out a disorderly member, by voice or with the gavel.

q1536.answer: To drown out a disorderly member.

sources.says: Nonmembers allowed in the hall as guests have no rights with respect to the proceedings. The chair can protect the assembly from annoyance by them.

q1537.answer: They have no rights in the proceedings.

sources.says: If a member is expelled after trial, the society may disclose that fact as far as needed for protection, but no one may make public the charge the member was found guilty of.
Witnesses at a society’s trial are not sworn.
A resolution to appoint an investigating committee is offered when nonmembers are not present.

q1538.answer: The false statement is that the society may tell anyone why an expelled member was found guilty.

sources.says: The steps of a fair disciplinary process are: a confidential investigation by a committee, the committee’s report with charges if warranted, formal notice to the accused, a trial, and the assembly’s review of a trial committee’s findings.

q1539.answer: A confidential investigation by a committee.

sources.says: If the organization’s rules don’t provide a method of charge and trial, a member may, when nonmembers aren’t present, offer a resolution to appoint an investigating committee.

q1540.answer: A member should offer a resolution to appoint an investigating committee.

sources.says: An investigating committee has no power to require the accused or anyone else to appear before it, but it should quietly conduct a complete investigation and try to learn all relevant facts.

q1541.answer: Require the accused to appear before it.

sources.says: The “managers” present the evidence against the accused and must be members of the society. Their duty isn’t to act as prosecutors seeking conviction, but to help the trial get at the truth.

q1542.answer: They present the evidence against the accused.

sources.says: The secretary sends the accused a letter giving the date, hour, and place of the trial, an exact copy of the charges and specifications, and a direction to appear as cited.
Nonmembers who agree to testify can be brought in as witnesses, but are allowed in the room only while testifying.

After some preliminaries (noting that the meeting is in executive session, reading the resolutions about the trial, confirming the accused received the charges, announcing the managers, and asking whether the accused has counsel), the trial proceeds in order. First, the secretary reads the charge and specifications. Second, the chair asks the accused how they plead, guilty or not guilty. A guilty plea means no trial is needed; after a plea of not guilty come opening statements, witnesses, and the rest.

q1545.answer: Asking the accused how they plead is the second step.

sources.says: After a guilty finding, most penalties, including removal from office, need a majority vote. Expulsion requires a two-thirds vote.
A standing Committee on Discipline is normally charged with watching for disciplinary problems, investigating them, introducing resolutions, and managing any trial.
If it also hears the trial, it’s generally best not to empower it to impose a penalty, but to report its recommendation to the assembly.
A standing Committee on Discipline normally investigates disciplinary problems, introduces the necessary resolutions, and manages the case at trial.
A main motion can be made only while no other motion is pending.
The Previous Question can be applied to an immediately pending motion that is debatable or amendable, or to a series of such motions.

q1550.answer: When the immediately pending motion can’t be debated or amended.

sources.says: Postpone Indefinitely takes precedence over nothing except the main question. It is the lowest-ranking subsidiary motion and can only be made while the main question is immediately pending.
Ordering the Previous Question prevents any further subsidiary motions except Lay on the Table.
Postpone Indefinitely is applied to the main question and takes precedence over nothing else.

sources.section: §15 Limit or Extend Limits of Debate
sources.says: Limit or Extend Limits of Debate can be made only while a debatable motion is immediately pending. It yields to Lay on the Table and to all privileged motions, which aren’t debatable.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says proposals for filling a blank are adopted by a majority vote.
Motions relating to nominations need a majority, except a motion to close nominations, which requires two-thirds.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says creating a blank needs only a majority.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says a motion to refer a matter that isn’t pending is a main motion. It’s out of order when another has the floor, must be seconded, is debatable and amendable, and needs a majority.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says a motion to depart immediately from an adopted convention agenda is incidental, out of order when another has the floor, not debatable, not amendable, and needs two-thirds.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says a main motion to limit or extend debate for the duration of a meeting is debatable, amendable, can be reconsidered, and requires a two-thirds vote.

q1558.answer: It is never adopted by a mere majority.

sources.section: §22 Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn
sources.says: A motion to fix the time to which to adjourn made when no question is pending is debatable and follows the other rules for main motions.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules lists it as amendable, out of order when another has the floor, and needing a majority.
Motions relating to nominations are out of order when another has the floor or a member is making a nomination. They aren’t debatable, are amendable, and need a majority except to close nominations.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says nominations can’t be made when another has the floor.

q1560.answer: They are never in order when another member has the floor.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says Lay on the Table must be seconded and isn’t debatable or amendable.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table says Postpone to a Certain Time must be seconded.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table says Postpone Indefinitely must be seconded and isn’t amendable.
A Point of Order is normally ruled on by the chair.
A Parliamentary Inquiry is directed to the presiding officer, whose duty is to answer it.

q1562.answer: They are both decided by the chair.

sources.says: Raise a Question of Privilege is a privileged device that ranks just below Recess, Adjourn, and Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn.

sources.section: §6 Description of Classes and Individual Motions
sources.says: Questions of privilege can also be brought up as main motions when no motion is pending.
Any member can move that permission to read a paper be granted. The motion needs no second unless it is moved by the member who made the request.

Reconsideration in a standing or special committee differs from reconsideration in the assembly: it can be moved no matter how much time has passed, and a question can be reconsidered any number of times; any committee member who did not vote on the losing side may move it, even one who didn’t vote or was absent; and it needs a two-thirds vote unless every member who voted on the prevailing side is present or was given reasonable notice that it would be moved.
Among the standard characteristics of Reconsider: it is not amendable, and a vote on a motion to Reconsider cannot itself be reconsidered.
The relaxed procedures used in small boards apply in the meetings of all standing and special committees, unless the committee has been instructed otherwise.
One of those relaxed procedures is that motions do not need to be seconded.

q1565.answer: The false statement is that it always needs a two-thirds vote. Two-thirds is needed only when a member who voted on the winning side is absent and wasn’t notified. The other statements are all true in a committee.

sources.says: For committee reports, the expressions adopt, accept, and agree to all mean the same thing: the text becomes the act or statement of the assembly.

q1566.answer: All three mean the same thing.

sources.says: When a blank exists, the chair calls for suggestions, and members simply suggest names, places, numbers, dates, or amounts to fill it.
If there’s an objection to reading, any member can move that permission to read be granted, including the member who wants to read.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says such a motion can be made by the person requesting permission or by another member.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says motions relating to voting made while a question is pending are incidental motions. They must be seconded, aren’t debatable, and are amendable.
When nominations from the floor are called for, a member rises and says “I nominate Mr. A.”
A Parliamentary Inquiry is a question to the presiding officer for information on parliamentary law or the organization’s rules bearing on the business at hand.
A member calling another member to order rises and, without waiting for recognition, says “Mr. President, I call the member to order,” then sits down.

q1572.answer: They don’t need recognition from the chair.

sources.says: Societies generally provide in their bylaws for a board empowered to act for them between regular meetings. It is usually called the executive board.
If only one person is nominated and the bylaws don’t require a ballot, the chair makes sure no one else wants to nominate and simply declares the nominee elected by unanimous consent.
In a voice election with more than one nominee, candidates are voted on in the order nominated.

q1574.answer: Dunbar’s key says any of these: vote on the presidential nominee, vote on the vice-presidential nominee, or declare them elected.
q1574.conflict: RONR 12th ed. calls for the chair to declare a sole nominee elected by acclamation rather than take a vote (46:40). Taking a vote isn’t the procedure the book describes for this case.

sources.section: List IV, Motions and Parliamentary Steps by Floor and Second
sources.says: RONR’s list of motions by floor and second places Objection to the Consideration of a Question among those in order when another has been assigned the floor but hasn’t begun to speak.

sources.section: §26 Objection to the Consideration of a Question
sources.says: An Objection to the Consideration of a Question doesn’t require a second and isn’t debatable.

q1575.answer: Objection to the Consideration of a Question.

sources.says: Two degrees of amendment are possible: a primary amendment to the pending motion and a secondary amendment to the primary.
A third-degree amendment isn’t permitted.

q1576.answer: One primary and one secondary amendment.

sources.says: In the president’s absence, or when the president vacates the chair, the vice-president serves in the president’s place.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says a motion to adjourn made as a main motion must be seconded, is debatable and amendable, needs a majority, and can’t be reconsidered.

sources.section: §62 Removal from Office and Other Remedies for Dereliction of
sources.says: If the chair culpably fails to perform the duties of the chair properly in a meeting, the assembly may take measures to replace the chair temporarily with another presiding officer.
When a motion censures the presiding officer, the chair should hand the chair to the vice-president or a temporary occupant while it is considered.

q1579.answer: Move to censure the presiding officer.

sources.says: A special (select, or ad hoc) committee is appointed for a specific task and ceases to exist when it presents its final report.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says a Parliamentary Inquiry needs no second, isn’t voted on but answered by the chair, and has no reconsideration.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table says a Request for Information needs no second, isn’t voted on, and can’t be reconsidered.
Without a quorum, the assembly may fix the time to which to adjourn, adjourn, recess, or take measures to obtain a quorum.
The president or chief officer of an organized society who normally presides is addressed as “Mr. President” or “Madam President,” or by the official title.

For an offense against the assembly in a meeting, no formal trial is needed if a penalty is imposed promptly, since the witnesses are present. The chair alone can’t impose a penalty or order a member removed.

q1584.answer: No formal trial with witnesses is needed.

sources.says: Rejecting a motion to Amend leaves the pending motion worded as it was before the amendment was voted on.

q1585.answer: Worded as it was before the amendment.

sources.says: A Division may be demanded from when the negative votes are cast until the result is announced, or immediately afterward.
It is too late once the chair has stated the question on another motion made afterward.

q1586.answer: Until the chair states the question on another motion.

sources.says: Large boards generally follow parliamentary procedure the same way as any other assembly. Small boards and committees allow some informality.
A committee large enough to function like a full assembly should be instructed to follow the regular rules.

q1587.answer: In the same way as any assembly.

sources.says: Any member may give notice of a bylaw amendment unless the bylaws limit who can. It is usually given under new business.

sources.section: §59 Organization of a Convention of an Established Society
sources.says: A sample convention rule requires a resolution offered by a member to be in writing and signed by the maker and seconder.

q1588.answer: Dunbar’s key says it should be signed by the mover and seconder.
q1588.conflict: RONR 12th ed. doesn’t prescribe who signs a written notice of a bylaw amendment. Signing by the maker and seconder appears only in its sample convention rule for resolutions (59:41), so treat this as Dunbar’s guidance.

sources.says: Ordinary societies often use an auditing committee of members. In some organizations, financial reports are audited by elected officers called “trustees.”
If a main motion is referred while Postpone Indefinitely is pending, that motion is ignored and doesn’t go to the committee, because referral shows the assembly doesn’t favor it.

q1590.answer: Declare that the motion to Postpone Indefinitely won’t be considered.

sources.says: All privileged motions are undebatable, because debate would let their high privilege interfere with business.

sources.section: §26 Objection to the Consideration of a Question
sources.says: An Objection to the Consideration of a Question doesn’t require a second, isn’t debatable, and isn’t amendable.
When the chair appoints or nominates a committee, the chair picks its chairman by naming that person first.
An affirmative vote on Lay on the Table can’t be reconsidered, because taking the question from the table is simpler.

sources.section: Table II, Table of Rules Relating to Motions
sources.says: The table of rules says Postpone to a Certain Time can be reconsidered. Amend and the Previous Question can also be reconsidered.

sources.section: §5 Basic Classifications; Order of Precedence of Motions
sources.says: A secondary motion, such as a subsidiary motion like Amend or the Previous Question, can be made while a main motion is pending.
The privileged motion to Adjourn takes precedence over all motions except Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn.
Postpone Indefinitely takes precedence over nothing except the main question. It yields to all other subsidiary motions, all privileged motions, and applicable incidental motions.
RONR’s example of a main motion with a pending amendment shows that referral to a committee, Lay on the Table, and Recess can all be moved at that point.

q1596.conflict: Under RONR 12th ed., Postpone Indefinitely is out of order while an amendment is immediately pending, because it ranks below Amend. Lay on the Table, Recess, and Refer to a Committee are all in order then (10:34).

sources.says: Postpone Indefinitely is debatable, with debate going into the main question, but it isn’t amendable.

q1597.answer: Postpone Indefinitely (the question means “not amendable but debatable”).

sources.says: If the affirmative leads by one without the chair’s vote, the chair can vote in the negative to create a tie. A tie means the motion is lost.

q1598.answer: A tie, 24 to 24, so the main motion is lost.

sources.section: §18 Call for the Orders of the Day
sources.says: When a member starts a motion departing from the correct order of business, and no special order is involved, the call must be made before the chair states the motion.

q1599.answer: Before the chair states the motion.

sources.says: A question laid on the table can be taken up in the same session, or at the next regular session if it comes within a quarterly time interval. Otherwise it dies, though it can be reintroduced later as a new question.

q1600.answer: None of these. With a year between meetings the tabled motion has died, so it must be introduced again as a new motion.

sources.section: §15 Limit or Extend Limits of Debate
sources.says: When an order limiting or extending debate no longer applies to any of the motions it affected, it is said to be “exhausted.”
To make a main motion, a member who has the floor says, in simple cases, “I move that…,” followed by the proposed wording.
A member offering a motion should avoid saying “I so move” and should state the complete motion.
A member who wants the motion considered says “I second the motion,” “I second it,” or even “Second!” without obtaining the floor.

sources.section: §44 Bases for Determining a Voting Result
sources.says: A majority vote means more than half of the votes cast by those entitled to vote.

q1604.answer: 16, since more than half of 30 is 16.

sources.says: A special (select, or ad hoc) committee is appointed for a specific task and ceases to exist when it presents its final report.
A committee, except a committee of the whole, can appoint subcommittees. They are responsible and report to the committee, not the assembly.
A motion made on behalf of a board or properly appointed committee needs no second from the floor, as long as the group has more than one person.

q1607.conflict: RONR 12th ed. says a committee’s motion needs no second when the committee has more than one person (4:11). Only a one-person committee’s motion needs a second.

sources.says: The power to appoint a committee includes the power to fill any vacancy in it.
When the details of an adopted motion to refer are being filled in, the member who made the motion has no preference in recognition, since they could have included the details.

q1609.answer: They have no preference in recognition.

sources.says: When a special committee has completed its business, it “rises” and reports, which is equivalent to the main motion to adjourn sine die.

sources.section: §52 Committee of the Whole and Its Alternate Forms
sources.says: A committee of the whole rises and reports when it has finished its work, when it wants to end the meeting, or when it wants action it can’t take itself.

q1610.answer: Dunbar’s key says the main motion to adjourn.
q1610.conflict: RONR 12th ed. describes rising as equivalent to adjourning sine die for a special committee (21:9). A committee of the whole rises so the assembly can resume and receive its report, which isn’t an adjournment of the assembly.
